Article Title: Parliament monsoon session yet to be prorogued, BJP, Congress face off over women’s bill
Article Text:
BJP steps up attack on Rahul Gandhi over women’s quota, accusing Congress of blocking early implementation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: BJP on Sunday sought to play back to Rahul Gandhi his pitch for women’s empowerment, by questioning his strident opposition to govt’s push for an early implementation of quota for them in Lok Sabha and assemblies.“He does not want to give rights to women. His words don’t match his actions,” Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis said.BJP’s framing its attack on Rahul around the women’s quota coupled with the fact that monsoon session is yet to be prorogued gave another indication of the possibility of govt summoning the two Houses at short notice to take up its Constitution amendment bill for implementation of quota from 2029 with a nearly 50% rise in Lok Sabha seats.“What explains the abnormal delay now? Is the Union home minister still in search of his super-tainted 2/3rd majority to get the constitutional amendment bill on delimitation passed in a special session,” Congress’s Jairam Ramesh asked.Congress, too, was mindful of the possibility of a short upcoming session and claimed that BJP is still searching for “super tainted” majority in Lok Sabha, in what was a swipe at govt’s alleged attempts to split opposition parties to reach the two-thirds majority in the House needed for the bill’s passage.Ramesh said the gap between Parliament’s adjournment and its prorogation is generally two to four days. But the monsoon session, which ended on Aug 13, has not been prorogued yet.When a session is prorogued, govt has to go through the protocol for calling a new session that conventionally requires a gap of 15 to 20 days.Stepping up BJP’s attack on Rahul Gandhi, Fadnavis said he spoke about women’s empowerment from a public platform but has opposed the most revolutionary step to give women their due.BJP’s Smriti Irani said Rahul should positively respond to PM Modi’s appeal to political parties to support the implementation of women’s quota. On the Vande Mataram row, she said Congress should allow rendition of the song’s full version.While speculation has swirled over the revival of the bill to amend women’s quota law, which was defeated in April, govt has officially remained non-committal over any such move except acknowledging that it had sought Rahul’s view. The LoP in Lok Sabha reiterated his stand against it. Congress and its allies have said Lok Sabha’s strength should be frozen at its existing number and the quota should be executed within it.
Article Summary: BJP steps up attack on Rahul Gandhi over women’s quota, accusing Congress of blocking early implementation of quota. Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis: “He does not want to give rights to women. His words don’t match his actions,”

Article Title: 'Killed Nijjar for drug trafficking': Goldy Brar in leaked audio
Article Text:
Leaked audio captures Goldy Brar claiming Nijjar was targeted over alleged drug trafficking and its impact on young people

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a leaked audio conversation with pro-Khalistan terrorist Paramjit Singh Pamma, US-based gangster Goldy Brar has admitted to orchestrating the murder of Hardeep Singh Nijjar, a pro-Khalistan terrorist, in Canada in June 2023.Brar said Nijjar, whose killing had triggered a diplomatic crisis between India and Canada, was targeted over his "involvement in drug trafficking and promoting drug abuse". Intelligence sources confirmed the voice in the audio was Brar's.Brar, wanted in India for several killings - including that of singer Sidhu Moosewala - is heard saying Nijjar's promotion of drugs among teens irked him.This admission surfaced alongside the execution of Operation Hardball, a joint US-Canada law enforcement crackdown targeting transnational crime syndicates. The investigation had indicted Brar and Lawrence Bishnoi for orchestrating the killing of ‘HSN’ (short for Nijjar), reframing the high-profile assassination as a gangland hit rather than a state-sponsored killing.“Those who groomed and incited 16-to-17-year-olds to sell drugs... those who blackmailed young people into selling drugs and becoming informants... Nijjar supported and strengthened these individuals so that he could use them when necessary,” Brar is heard telling Pamma.“That’s why me and my team had to kill Nijjar, because these people were using young people to sell drugs. Good or bad, everyone has to face the consequences of their actions,” he added.Brar’s admission, which comes after his and Lawrence’s Op Hardball indictment in Nijjar’s murder, also reflected in Canadian police’s initial probe which hinted at gang rivalry. The probe also noted that a hit on Nijjar had been circulating for several weeks on an encrypted online site used to hire hitmen.Nijjar (45) was shot on June 18, 2023, in the parking lot of Guru Nanak Sikh Gurdwara, in Newton, Surrey. Six men and two vehicles were used in the attack. A CCTV video showed Nijjar’s grey pickup truck and a white sedan driving parallel in the parking lot of the gurdwara, seconds before the shooting started.Nijjar, the head of Khalistan Tiger Force (KTF), was replaced by his confidant Arshdeep Singh alias Arsh Dala. Interestingly, in the latest audio, Brar is also heard claiming the killing of Dala’s close associate, Sukhdool Singh alias Sukha Duneke, who was murdered in Winnipeg area in Sept 2023.
Article Summary: Leaked audio captures Goldy Brar claiming Nijjar was targeted over alleged drug trafficking and its impact on young people. Intelligence sources confirmed the voice in the audio was Brar's. Brar is wanted in India for several killings - including that of singer Sidhu Moosewala.

Article Title: Many poor in queue, can't allow 'luxury litigation' by rich: SC
Article Text:
SC slams ‘luxury litigation’, says 11-year legal battle delayed genuine cases; imposes Rs 5 lakh cost each

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: At a time when poor litigants have to wait in line for years to get their plea heard, Supreme Court Friday disapproved the practice of influential people indulging in "luxury litigation", resulting in hearing of genuine cases getting delayed. It imposed a cost of Rs 5 lakh each on warring litigants for not approaching the court with "clean hands".A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta rejected the plea of actress Rehana Khan and her lawyer Rizwan Siddique who have been fighting legal battles for past 11 years before different forums, including Bar Council of India, Bombay HC and SC."Each of these parties has come to us complaining of a wrong, and each has been the author of a good part of it. Between them, they have occupied the time of the Bar Council, an HC and this court for 11 years. That time belonged to other litigants, waiting for relief they genuinely needed. We record our strong disapproval of the conduct of both. In view of the conduct of each party, we find it fit to impose costs," the bench said.The bench noted that the two litigants approached the court in the confident expectation of vindication."Every fact of consequence has had to be prised out of a record in which suppression, embellishment and afterthought are the common currency of both sides. The machinery of justice is not a facility placed at the disposal of parties to settle scores, to salvage reputations they have themselves imperilled, or to extract advantage from a controversy of their own making.We say at the outset, and give our reasons in what follows, that neither the appellant nor the respondent leaves this court with credit," it said."Record in these matters makes for compelling reading. Litigation of this kind holds a certain fascination, and we do not pretend otherwise. But a court is not an auditorium, and the drama of a case is no measure of its merit. Stripped of its theatre, what these proceedings disclose is a controversy which two litigants have between them manufactured, prolonged and brought to the highest court in the country, each in the hope that we would be sufficiently diverted by the spectacle to overlook their own part in creating it. We have not been," it said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court disapproves the practice of influential people indulging in "luxury litigation" It imposed a cost of Rs 5 lakh each on warring litigants for not approaching the court with "clean hands" A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta rejected the plea of actress Rehana Khan.

Article Title: 'We fought wars with Pakistan too, but China will be India's main competitor': Ex-Army chief
Article Text:
General MM Naravane (Retd) on China and Pakistan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Army chief General MM Naravane (Retired) on Thursday described China as India's "main competitor" in the years ahead, despite India having fought wars with both China and Pakistan."Pakistan and China are a totally different ballgame. We have fought wars with both of them. We have unsettled borders. So they will always remain on our radar as a threat, as a challenge," PTI quoted Naravane as saying at a book launch event in New Delhi.However, he distinguished between the two, saying India's immediate focus on Pakistan was driven largely by the continuing threat of terrorism, while describing China as a "competitor" rather than an "enemy." He emphasised that he had "purposely" used the term "competitor" for China."We have fought major wars with Pakistan, and because of their continued support to terrorism, our attention is towards our western borders. But I think we are very clear that in the long term and in the years to come, China is going to be our main competitor. And I purposely use the word competitor and not enemy," Naravane said.Naravane, who was Chief of Army Staff during the 2020 Ladakh clashes with China and led India's response, further stated that the two countries would be competitors across multiple domains, including politics, economics, trade and military affairs."They are going to be our main competitor in all fields. Political, economic, trade, and of course military also. And wherever there is competition, there is always a little bit of conflict," the retired Army general observed.He emphasised that India should seek to manage such differences through dialogue and diplomatic mechanisms rather than resorting to force."It is up to us to try to resolve those conflicts, those differences, through the mechanisms of talks, dialogues. And taking recourse to the use of force should always be the last priority," he said.However, he also stressed that India must maintain credible military preparedness to deter any potential misadventure."There comes a moment when you realise that this is not going to happen. And therefore, you have to have a strong deterrence. That is why the armed forces have to be ready at all times. You have to have a strong deterrence to stop anybody from taking recourse to the use of force or any misadventure," he remarked.
Article Summary: Former Army chief describes China as India's "main competitor" despite India having fought wars with both China and Pakistan. He distinguished between the two, saying India's immediate focus on Pakistan was driven largely by the continuing threat of terrorism. He emphasised that he had "purposely" used the term "competitor" for China.

Article Title: Ex-IAF vice-chief Kapoor says India’s 4.5-gen Tejas may not have relevance in 2030s, country must partner with global consortiums like FCAS or GCAP for 6th-gen programme
Article Text:
Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) did not totally rule out the role of Tejas Mk2 in future

NEW DELHI: Less than two months after retirement as the IAF's vice chief, Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor (Retd) has slammed the delay in the delivery of Tejas (LCA) fighter jet by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited to the air force, saying, “why must it be that a machine that was promised to us so many years back with a certain set of capabilities continues to be denied to us on one pretext or the other”.In an interview to NDTV, the IAF veteran said, “Why must we be hamstrung because someone somewhere has not been able to keep their promises?”The delivery of the indigenous LCA Tejas Mk1A jets by HAL to the IAF has faced multi-year delays, primarily caused by late supplies of F404-IN20 engines by American GE company, complex mission software validation, and stringent operational requirements set by the IAF.When asked if advanced Tejas Mk-2 may be operationally relevant when it starts entering service in big numbers in mid 2030s at a time when China is already raising its fleet of its 5th-generation fighter jet, the former vice-chief said, “No, operationally, definitely no.”With China on its way to deploying 500 5th-generation J-20 fighters by 2030, India is still struggling to get the delivery of the first squadron by 4.5-generation Tejas Mk1A. Though the IAF had placed orders for a total of 180 Tejas Mk1A fighter jets long ago, HAL hopes to deliver the first 18-25 Tejas Mk1A only by March 2027.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) did not totally rule out the role of Tejas Mk2 in future when he said, “You can have a certain number of those 5th generation and 6th generation fighters, but given the size of the country, you won't be able to deploy them everywhere.So those gaps which continue to remain to be filled will have to be filled by this class of aircraft.” “I want Tejas Mk-2 to come, I want India’s 5th-gen AMCA to come. But they must come at a much faster speed,” he said.When asked about Russia’s 5th-gen fighter jet Su-57, the former vice-chief said when the Russian fighter is compared to western jets like American F-35, western jets have an edge over the Su-57 as they have better avionics and stealth.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) suggested that India should partner with an European consortium working on state-of-the-art sixth generation platforms. “There are other things that are happening — why not join FCAS (Future Combat Air System is the European programme for 6th generation jet under development by French Dassault Aviation, Airbus and Indra Sistemas) Why not GCAP (Global Combat Air Programme is a multinational initiative led by Italy, Japan, and UK to jointly develop a sixth-generation jet).“'You are probably going with a consortium which has got a good record of delivery, of development. Why go through this Gen 4, Gen 4.5 steps when you know the next best thing is already being thought of and why not just join up there?,” the IAF veteran said.His comments underline the difficult choices facing India’s air power planners: meeting immediate squadron requirements while ensuring that indigenous programmes do not fall behind the rapid evolution of military aviation technology.
Article Summary: Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor (Retd) has slammed the delay in the delivery of Tejas (LCA) fighter jet by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited to the air force. “Why must it be that a machine that was promised to us so many years back with a certain set of capabilities continues to be denied to us on one pretext or the other” he said.

Article Title: Ex-diplomat Navdeep Suri flags 'trouble establishing citizenship' during Punjab SIR
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Former diplomat Navdeep Suri on Sunday said he was facing "trouble establishing his citizenship" during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Punjab, despite having represented India in three countries.In a post on X, Suri shared his experience with the voter roll revision and said he was asked to provide "unspecified documents" to establish that he was an Indian citizen."Sharing my experience with #SIR in Punjab. Went to BLO, submitted Voter ID and Aadhaar card, was assured that everything is in order. Got a message today from a volunteer saying some details don’t match with SIR in 2003!" Suri said.He said that after speaking to the booth-level officer (BLO), he was asked to collect a notice and return with documents proving his citizenship."Spoke with BLO, was told that I should come and collect the notice. And then come again with unspecified documents that show I am an Indian citizen. Replied that I was not in India in 2003, so they’ve asked for passport as proof," he added.Suri said he had documents apart from his voter ID and Aadhaar, but questioned what the process would mean for ordinary citizens."I happen to have documents other than voter ID and Aadhaar card.But can’t help asking: If I have trouble establishing my citizenship after representing India in three countries, what’s the fate of the common citizen? Ease of Living, I presume!" he said.Former ambassador Navdeep Suri has served as India's high commissioner to Australia and ambassador to UAE and Egypt.The SIR was first launched in Bihar in June 2025. Following the exercise, more than 60 lakh names, including those of deceased voters, were removed from the electoral rolls. In West Bengal, around 90 lakh voters were deleted from the rolls ahead of the assembly elections.Under the SIR process, voters who were not included in the 2002 or 2003 electoral rolls are required to submit documents linking them to people included in those legacy rolls. The Election Commission of India (ECI) had initially listed 11 acceptable documents, excluding Aadhaar.Following proceedings in the Supreme Court , the poll panel expanded the list to include Aadhaar as an acceptable document.The Supreme Court has also made observations on the broader constitutional implications of the exercise, stressing that while the ECI has the power to revise electoral rolls, those powers cannot be "untrammelled" and must comply with principles of transparency and natural justice.
Article Summary: Navdeep Suri has served as India's high commissioner to Australia and ambassador to UAE and Egypt. Suri shared his experience with the voter roll revision in Punjab. He said he was asked to provide "unspecified documents" to establish that he was an Indian citizen.

Article Title: 'Politics is art of possible': JD(U) leader hopes Nishant becomes CM like Nitish
Article Text:
Praising Nitish Kumar's record as Bihar chief minister, Thakur said he hoped his son would also make a mark in public life.

Thakur backs Nishant's political future

Nishant's performance as health minister

Senior JD(U) leader Devesh Chandra Thakur has expressed hope that Bihar health minister Nishant Kumar will follow the political path of his father, Nitish Kumar, and eventually rise to become the state's chief minister.Thakur made the remarks on Sunday while responding to questions from journalists in Sitamarhi, his Lok Sabha constituency. Nishant was visiting the district at the time and received a warm reception from JD(U) workers.Praising Nitish Kumar's record as Bihar chief minister, Thakur said he hoped his son would also make a mark in public life."Our leader Nitish Kumar has done a lot for Bihar. His two-decade-long tenure as chief minister remains unparalleled. We hope that Nishant would follow in the footsteps of his father and win accolades in public life," Thakur said.Asked directly whether he considered Nishant a possible future chief minister, Thakur replied, "Why not? Politics is the art of the possible. May he rise to the greatest heights."The remarks come months after Nishant, 45, entered politics in March this year. His entry came shortly before Nitish decided to contest the Rajya Sabha polls, bringing an end to his roughly two-decade tenure as Bihar chief minister.Nishant, who has generally maintained a low-key public profile, initially declined an offer to become deputy chief minister in the new Bihar government led by BJP's Samrat Choudhary. He later joined the cabinet as a minister following pressure from JD(U) workers and leaders.When Thakur was asked to assess Nishant's performance as health minister, he said it was too early to judge him."The young leader has just started off. It is rather childish to ask such a question at this juncture."During his visit to Sitamarhi, Nishant said he was happy to be in the district and spoke about his desire to serve people across different sections of society."I am thrilled to visit Sitamarhi, the place where Goddess Sita was believed to have been discovered. I pray to her that I live up to the expectations of the people and work for every section of the society, be it women, OBCs or EBCs, just like my father had done."JD(U) workers who attended the event said Nishant's emergence had eased concerns over a possible leadership vacuum following Nitish Kumar's withdrawal from active politics.They expressed confidence that the party would remain in safe hands under Nishant's leadership.
Article Summary: Senior JD(U) leader Devesh Chandra Thakur has expressed hope that Bihar health minister Nishant Kumar will follow the political path of his father, Nitish Kumar. He made the remarks on Sunday while responding to questions from journalists in Sitamarhi, his Lok Sabha constituency. Nishant, 45, entered politics in March this year.

Article Title: How Ananta Maharaj row exposed old fault lines over Netaji
Article Text:
Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose

The 'war criminal' letter

Conundrum

What Nehru said on Netaji

Congress: from president to rebel

An Indian Pilgrim

The Indian Struggle

From comrades to 'Fifth Column'

How INA played a key role

Samik, Forward Bloc and another old rivalry

Renkoji: the argument that never ended

Renkoji temple

From debating Bose to claiming Bose

PM Modi unveiling Netaji statue

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For the longest time, January 23 in 1990s Kolkata would mean small street-side political meetings where leaders of all hues would ask the youth to draw inspiration from Netaji's patriotism and ideals on his birthday. Netaji was one of the most prominent politicians who disappeared before India became independent, and yet left a firm imprint on people's minds. The conversation around him was often about what people knew and what, they believed, had been concealed, be it the mystery surrounding his disappearance, the classified files or his political views, which parties have tried to appropriate and yet conveniently stayed away from at different times. His own political party, the Forward Bloc, a junior partner in the long-running Left Front government in West Bengal, is now a pale shadow of its glory days. Yet Netaji remains an iconic hero not only in Bengal but across India. BJP Rajya Sabha MP Nagendra Ray, better known as Ananta Maharaj, has apologised for his vitriolic remarks on Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose. The dust will settle soon, but what is unlikely to be ironed out any time soon is the uneasy relationship political parties in Bengal have had with the state's most enduring nationalist icon.Ananta Maharaj rattled the hornet's nest by questioning Bose's contribution to the freedom struggle and the Indian National Army, was reported to have called him a "war criminal", and claimed the INA consisted essentially of British-Indian soldiers "captured and handed over by Germany". He also asked what the INA had achieved for Indian independence. This prompted swift action, with the Suvendu Adhikari government withdrawing the Banga Bibhushan , Bengal's highest civilian honour, which Mamata Banerjee's government had conferred on him. Subsequently, Ananta apologised.As a parting shot, the Rajya Sabha MP insisted his claims rested on material in the National Archives and invoked Jawaharlal Nehru over the "war criminal" description. This calls for a dispassionate look at what history actually says about these claims.Material declassified in 2016 revived a long-circulating claim that Nehru had called Bose Britain's "war criminal". The files contained a later account of an alleged Nehru dictation, not an authenticated original Nehru-to-Attlee letter.The archival trail leads to testimony by Shyam Lal Jain, Nehru's former stenographer, who claimed decades afterwards that Nehru had dictated a December 1945 communication to British Prime Minister Clement Attlee referring to "Subhas Chandra Bose, your war criminal".Nehru's own recorded words point in the opposite direction. On August 29, 1945, when an American journalist put it to him that Bose should be treated as a war criminal, Nehru replied: "I resent the suggestion that Subhas Bose should be dealt with as a war criminal." In April 1956, Nehru would again write internally that "the question of War Criminals does not arise" while discussing the Netaji inquiry.There is, however, an intriguing archival footnote. In, Chandrachur Ghose and Anuj Dhar cite a 1956 Ministry of External Affairs file created after notices of parliamentary questions asking whether Bose was still regarded as a war criminal. The questions followed Forward Bloc leader Muthuramalingam Thevar's demand before the Netaji Inquiry Committee that the government clarify whether Bose's name figured on such a list.The first response recorded in the file came from historian Sarvepalli Gopal, then head of the MEA's Historical Division. After consulting the Law and Defence ministries, Gopal wrote: "All records related to Subhas Bose were destroyed in 1947, but as far as we know Bose was not publicly designated a war criminal." The Khosla inquiry would later record an even more categorical government position: inquiries with Indian missions indicated that Bose's name had never figured on a war-criminal list.Ghose, speaking to TOI, is equally categorical that he has found no archival evidence establishing that Bose was a war criminal. He points out, however, that such an allegation was indeed made on oath by a pendant before the Khosla Commission.One thing, though, Ananta Maharaj does get right, Bose did not create the first INA. The INA initially took shape in Japanese-controlled Southeast Asia in 1942 under Captain Mohan Singh, built around British Indian Army soldiers who had fallen into Japanese hands during the Malaya campaign and the fall of Singapore. It broke down amid disputes over Japanese control. Rash Behari Bose began reorganising the movement in early 1943. Subhas Bose arrived in Southeast Asia that July and took over, after which the INA expanded dramatically in scale and political clout. So while Netaji wasn't the founder, he became the beating heart of the INA.The BJP MP appears to have conflated two different episodes from Netaji's life in making his claim about Germany. Before reaching Southeast Asia, Bose had run a separate military project in Germany, the Indian Legion, drawing substantially on Indian prisoners of war captured by Axis forces in North Africa.Bose's quarrel with Congress had multiple layers, some driven by the power politics of the time and others by the ideological strands to which its top leaders belonged. Bose rose to the top of the party, becoming Congress president at Haripura in 1938 and standing for a second term the following year, when he defeated Pattabhi Sitaramayya, the candidate identified with Gandhi's camp, by 203 votes. Gandhi's response became the stuff of legend: Sitaramayya's defeat, he said, was "more mine than his".That was merely the start of the churn. Twelve of the 15 members of the Congress Working Committee resigned, the Tripuri session deepened the crisis, and Bose eventually stepped down. Nehru and Gandhi disagreed with his more confrontational line against Britain, yet Nehru was unhappy at the prospect of Bose simply being pushed out. In April 1939, he wrote to Gandhi that doing so would be "an exceedingly wrong step".The war drove the two much further apart. Bose read Britain's vulnerability as India's opportunity, a calculation that took him to Nazi Germany and then to Japanese-controlled Southeast Asia. Nehru fiercely opposed that route. His respect for Bose's patriotism, however, remained intact. Speaking on Bose's birthday in January 1946, he said: "I never for a moment doubted that he was a brave soldier in the struggle for freedom. " He praised the communal unity of the INA and called the force a "legend".Chandra Kumar Bose, Netaji's grand-nephew, makes another distinction. Recalling what his father Amiya Nath Bose, Sarat Bose's son and therefore Netaji's nephew told him, Chandra says Bose's dealings with Hitler and Tojo should not be confused with ideological admiration for either. According to him, Netaji did not like either leader; the alliances were instruments towards what he saw as the overriding objective of Indian independence. Chandra argues that Bose's ownandremain essential reading for anyone trying to understand his political philosophy.The INA lost the war but gained widespread acceptance afterwards. The Red Fort trials of Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Kumar Sahgal and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon in late 1945 produced an outpouring of public sympathy. Nehru joined their defence and donned the barrister's robes after decades away from legal practice.Chandra also points to a famous anecdote about former British PM Clement Attlee. In a letter written two decades after their meeting, P B Chakravartti, former acting governor of West Bengal, recalled Attlee telling him during a 1956 visit that the INA's impact on the loyalty of the armed forces, followed by the Royal Indian Navy revolt, had been important in Britain's decision to leave. When asked about Gandhi's influence on the final decision, Chakravartti recalled Attlee describing it as "minimal".Before the war, Bose occupied ground that overlapped with the Indian Left. He belonged to the radical wing of nationalism and worked at building alliances with communists and other Left formations in Bengal.The war ended that. Hitler's attack on the Soviet Union in June 1941 fundamentally changed the Communist reading of the conflict and, by the turn of 1941-42, the Communist Party had moved towards its "People's War" line. Bose was moving in the opposite direction, towards Axis help against Britain.P C Joshi's 1945 defence of the Communist position named the Forward Bloc, along with the Congress Socialist Party and Trotskyists, as groups that "made the Fifth Column, the agents of the Jap invader".The original wartime publication carrying the exact words "Tojo's dog" is harder to pin down. But when CPI general secretary A B Bardhan apologised in 2010 for the party's historical assessment of Bose, contemporary reports recalled that the undivided CPI had denounced him as an "imperialist agent" and "Tojo's dog".The rethink had started much earlier. Chandra Bose recalls Jyoti Basu publicly acknowledging the Communist misreading of Netaji. Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee followed in 2003, calling it a "great mistake" and saying,"I am apologising for our mistaken assessment of Netaji," while continuing to disagree with Bose's Axis strategy.The Ananta row was not the first this year to reopen Netaji-era wounds. In July, Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya called Forward Bloc members "goons" and alleged that they had pelted stones at Syama Prasad Mookerjee while he was addressing a gathering at Mohammed Ali Park during the 1940 Calcutta Corporation election. He also subsequently claimed that Mookerjee had appealed to Subhas and Sarat Bose over the condition of Hindus in eastern Bengal and received no response.Forward Bloc called Samik's account a distortion Ghose says the real history was more complicated. Before the 1940 Corporation election, there were negotiations for an understanding between Bose's camp and the Hindu Mahasabha. They failed. Bose's group subsequently entered into a municipal pact with the Muslim League in April 1940, a tactical arrangement that immediately became ammunition for his opponents.Bose and Mookerjee were certainly adversaries. Mookerjee's diary records Bose warning him that if he tried to build the Hindu Mahasabha as a rival organisation in Bengal, Bose would see it broken, "by force if need be". Yet Chandrachur Ghose and Chandra Bose agree on another aspect that is often lost in today's retelling that the two remained remarkably civil towards each other despite the ideological battle.Mookerjee had long-standing links with the Bose family, intervened with authorities over the treatment of Subhas and Sarat while they were detained, and his writings spoke of "admiration and affection" for Subhas alongside political disagreement.Chandra adds a family footnote. After Bose's expulsion from Presidency College, Sir Asutosh Mookerjee, Syama Prasad's father, played a role in enabling him to resume his studies. Bose ultimately entered Scottish Church College.Chandra also points to Syama Prasad's participation in Fazlul Huq's Bengal ministry. In other words, Bengal's politics in those years was full of tactical arrangements that don't align well with clean ideological lines drawn retrospectively.Ghose goes a step further, arguing that newspapers aligned with the pro-Gandhi camp, already hostile to Bose for creating a new political organisation, also helped amplify the Bose-Mookerjee rift.There is another Netaji dispute on which governments and even members of his own family have not always spoken in one voice, regarding the urn at Tokyo's Renkoji Temple, which is said to contain remains carried from Taipei following the reported plane crash of August 18, 1945.The majority report of the Shah Nawaz Committee and the later Khosla Commission supported the plane-crash account. Prime Minister Morarji Desai told Parliament in 1978 that contradictions and later material meant their conclusions could not be treated as decisive. The Justice M K Mukherjee Commission subsequently concluded that Bose was dead but had not died in the alleged plane crash and that the Renkoji remains were not his.Chandra Bose's own position has changed dramatically. He once questioned the crash theory, but after the declassification exercise came to the opposite conclusion. In 2024, he publicly said that the evidence from 10 national and international inquiries, taken together with the released files, convinced him that Netaji died in the August 18, 1945 crash. He now says Japan deserves credit for preserving the remains with dignity for eight decades, but that the time has come to bring them home.Ghose, in his conversation with TOI, called for an anthropological examination of the Renkoji material, saying conventional DNA recovery may no longer be viable and insisting that any examination should be conducted under neutral observation.In 2015, Mamata Banerjee's government released 64 Netaji files running to 12,744 pages and challenged the Centre to open its own records. The Modi government followed with a phased central release, beginning with 100 digitised files on January 23, 2016.Then came the wrangling over what to call his birth anniversary. The Left had Desh Prem Divas. Mamata chose Desh Nayak Diwas. The Centre declared January 23 Parakram Diwas in 2021. In 2022, Modi unveiled Bose's statue near India Gate and said Netaji had been forgotten after Independence, his ideas and even the symbols associated with him ignored.Chandra Bose says this is precisely the problem with the politics around historical icons that their names are invoked while their ideology is often ignored. He is dismissive of Samik Bhattacharya's recent comments about Forward Bloc. Why, he asks, must one leader be pulled down simply to prop up another?Parties of all hues have tried to appropriate different facets of Netaji's life. The BJP has highlighted his military courage and uncompromising nationalism. The Left can point to his socialism, and anti-imperialism. Congress has the bragging rights of Netaji having been its two-time president. Ghose puts the problem another way. Bose was, as the title of his biography has it, an "inconvenient nationalist". Allegiance to the nation, he says, was the one overriding constant in Bose's politics.That is what makes the Ananta Maharaj row worth more than a news cycle. While he lived, Bose was too difficult for any political establishment to hold comfortably. Since his disappearance, his legacy has been too valuable for any of them to concede.
Article Summary: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was one of the most prominent politicians who disappeared before India became independent. The conversation around him was often about what people knew and what, they believed, had been concealed. Material declassified in 2016 revived a long-circulating claim that Nehru had called Bose Britain's "war criminal"

Article Title: Invoking Mahatma Gandhi, BJP to start nationwide Vande campaign
Article Text:
The campaign was approved at a meet of new office-bearers Saturday

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Month-long campaign for PM Modi's birthday

NEW DELHI: BJP cited Mahatma Gandhi's "we have fallen on evil days" lament over the opposition built up against Vande Mataram Saturday to set the stage for an intense political battle with Congress and the wider 'secular' class for their objections to the national song's full version by announcing a nationwide campaign.The campaign, approved at a meeting of the new office-bearers under party chief Nitin Nabin, will focus on the song's association with freedom struggle, opposition by Pakistan's founder M A Jinnah and other Muslim hardliners which led Congress to prune it and "communal pressure or narrow vote-bank considerations" driving the current protests against the national song.The meeting adopted a four-page resolution, accusing Congress of "bowing before the same politics of appeasement" to which it had yielded in 1937, enabling Jinnah-led Muslim League to impose communal demands even upon national symbols.BJP's decision to launch the 10-point campaign comes after Congress asserted that it will stick to its 1937 resolution that had adopted the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram to signal its defiance of the notification restoring its full version for all official events and Parliament passing a law making any insult to the song a penal offence. With Gen Z emerging as an axis of political mobilisation for its rivals after their successful protest over paper leaks, the campaign also seeks to target its pitch for Vande Mataram at the youth.PM Modi visited party headquarters to interact with the new team. Organisational meetings are all about new ideas aimed at strengthening the party and deepening connection with the people, he said.In its resolution, BJP marshalled comments of stalwarts like Gandhi and C Rajagopalachari to hit back at its rivals, who have accused it of stoking political divide over the song. It framed its campaign as a contest between the song's rich legacy versus a bid to truncate it to appease Muslim fundamentalists.It cited Gandhi's 1939 comments: "I associated the purest national spirit with it (Vande Mataram). It never occurred to me that it was a Hindu song or meant only for Hindus. Unfortunately, now we have fallen on evil days." Nabin accused Congress of sowing the same seeds of division that it did in 1937 by adopting a truncated version under the Muslim League's pressure.Several youth-centric programmes will be part of BJP's month-long campaign from Modi's birthday on Sept 17, with the annual "sewa" programme turning special this time as he will also be completing 25 years as head of a govt.
Article Summary: Campaign will focus on song's association with freedom struggle, opposition by Pakistan's founder M A Jinnah and other Muslim hardliners. Meeting adopted a four-page resolution accusing Congress of "bowing before the same politics of appeasement" to which it had yielded in 1937.

Article Title: ‘If you can’t take it back, don’t say it’: Ajay Jadeja’s blunt message to Yashasvi Jaiswal after Asitha Fernando spat
Article Text:
India's Yashasvi Jaiswal, second right, and Sri Lanka's Asitha Fernando (78) exchange words. (AP Photo)

Jadeja warns Jaiswal over physical contact

India coach admits Jaiswal should have kept his distance

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Match referee could decide Jaiswal’s fate

NEW DELHI: Yashasvi Jaiswal ’s heated on-field confrontation with Sri Lanka pacer Asitha Fernando on the opening day of the second Test in Colombo drew criticism from former India all-rounder Ajay Jadeja , who warned the young opener that physical contact crosses a dangerous line.Jaiswal was dismissed for 45 by Fernando in the first session at the SSC ground after the Sri Lankan pacer had conceded three boundaries to the left-hander in the over. Fernando responded with a send-off as Jaiswal began walking back to the pavilion, prompting the India opener to turn around and confront the bowler.The exchange quickly escalated, with the two players trading words before coming face-to-face. Jaiswal’s helmet made contact with Fernando’s forehead, and there was also a push before Sri Lanka captain Dhananjaya de Silva and other players intervened to separate them.Jadeja, speaking on Sony Sports, criticised Jaiswal for taking the confrontation too far and drew a comparison with an earlier incident involving the Indian opener and Sri Lanka’s Niroshan Dickwella."It is dangerous territory. There is no doubt about that. Physical contact is a different thing. In the last match, Jaiswal was on the other side. He was fielding, and he said things to Niroshan Dickwella, and we said that banter is nice as long as there is nothing wrong with your language," Jadeja said on Sony Sports.He then stressed that players who engage in banter must also be prepared to receive it."The same thing happened, but if someone cannot laugh at himself, he shouldn't laugh at others. If you can't take it back, don't say it to others either while standing on the ground," he added.Jadeja's comments came after Jaiswal's confrontation with Fernando turned physical, putting the India batter under the scrutiny of match officials and potentially the ICC Code of Conduct.India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak also acknowledged that Jaiswal should not have moved so close to Fernando, although he suggested the exchange was the result of emotions running high."I think the bowler must have made some comment, and it was probably said in the heat of the moment. Obviously, I don't think Jaiswal should have gone that close, but these things happen in the heat of the moment," Kotak said.Kotak reiterated his assessment in the post-day press conference, saying the exchange could have been triggered by something Fernando said."I think they must have said something to him and it might have happened in the heat of the moment. Obviously, Jaiswal, I don't think he should have been so close (to Fernando), but that happens when you are in the heat of the moment," Kotak said.Sri Lanka fast bowling coach Ryan van Niekerk declined to comment on any possible punishment and left the matter to match referee Andy Pycroft.“The verbals are probably an overflow of emotion. I'll leave that to the match referee to deal with,” he said.Pycroft could examine the incident under Article 2.12 of the ICC Code of Conduct, which deals with “inappropriate physical contact” with another player during an international match.If Jaiswal is found guilty of a Level 1 offence, the possible punishment can range from an official reprimand to a fine of up to 50% of his match fee, along with one or two demerit points.
Article Summary: Jadeja warns Jaiswal over physical contact with Sri Lanka pacer Asitha Fernando. India batsman was dismissed for 45 by Fernando in the first session at the SSC ground. Fernando responded with a send-off, prompting the India opener to turn around and confront the bowler.

Article Title: Heartbreak for India as Australia advance to semifinals after goalless Hockey World Cup draw

India vs Australia Hockey (Photo by HI)

India push for winner, but Australia hold firm

India’s FIH Women's Hockey World Cup 2026 campaign came to a heartbreaking end as Australia held them to a 0-0 draw and advanced to the semifinals on Sunday. With the result, Australia progressed by virtue of having scored more goals in the pool, while India will now play for fifth place.Australia started strongly and appeared to take the lead in the second minute through Grace Stewart, but India immediately reviewed the goal for dangerous play. The referral went India’s way and the goal was ruled out.The Hockeyroos continued to control possession and created several opportunities, forcing Bichu Devi and Savita into important saves. India also struggled to retain the ball during the opening stages, although they gradually settled into the contest.Australia earned penalty corners but failed to convert, while India’s defence repeatedly managed to clear the danger. The first half ended goalless, despite India earning a penalty corner with just 21 seconds remaining.India came out with greater intensity after the break and began pressing Australia higher up the pitch. However, the Hockeyroos remained dangerous on the counter and continued to test the Indian defence.Australia thought they had finally broken the deadlock in the 40th minute when Kershaw found the net, but another review ruled that the ball had struck an Indian defender’s arm, making the goal illegal.The final quarter became increasingly tense. India created a promising opportunity when Navneet and Lalremsiami found themselves in the centre of the circle but failed to coordinate their attempt.Australia then earned further penalty corners, but India’s first rusher and goalkeeper Bichu Devi stood firm. Colwill’s drag-flick was blocked, while another Australian referral was rejected.With time running out, India removed Bichu Devi and brought on Deepika as an additional outfield player in a final attempt to find the winner. Australia, however, managed the closing stages smartly, keeping possession near the corners and running down the clock.The final whistle confirmed a 0-0 draw. Australia advanced to the semifinals, while India’s hopes of ending their 51-year wait for a World Cup semifinal appearance came to an end.
Article Summary: India's FIH Women's Hockey World Cup 2026 campaign came to a heartbreaking end as Australia held them to a 0-0 draw. With the result, Australia progressed by virtue of having scored more goals in the pool, while India will now play for fifth place.

Tempers were flying high moments after Asitha Fernando dismissed Yashasvi Jaiswal off the last delivery of the 17th over. It was already an eventful over with three boundaries, concluding dramatically when the bowler had the last laugh as Jaiswal inside-edged the delivery back onto his stumps. Disappointed, the left-hander started walking back to the dressing room when something during the animated send-off triggered him, and he instantly returned.The 24-year-old charged toward the bowler, making visible contact with Fernando's head. The Sri Lankan players stepped in, separated the two and prevented the situation from escalating. India's batting coach Sitanshu Kotak felt Jaiswal shouldn't have gone so close and termed the incident as something that happened in the "heat of the moment"."I think the bowler commented something and it happened in the heat of moment. Obviously Yashasvi shouldn’t have gone so close to him but it happened in the heat of the moment," said Kotak.Sri Lanka bowling coach Ryan van Niekerk also downplayed the incident, leaving it to the match referee to deal with."Look it is hard Test cricket, isn't it? When you're coming up against a team like India, you can't sit on the back foot and just bowl at them.I think from our side, it's bringing the challenge all the time, trying to make sure we can create something," said Ryan van Niekerk."And so, from my point of view, I've really asked the bowlers to stand up and create something. The verbals are probably an overflow of emotion. I'll leave that to the match referee to deal with," he added.It now remains to be seen how ICC match referee Andy Pycroft views the incident. Clear video evidence of the physical contact exists and could invite sanctions ranging from a reprimand to a 50% match fee and demerit points. Article 2.12 of the ICC Code of Conduct deals with "inappropriate physical contact"."Inappropriate physical contact with a Player, Player Support Personnel, Umpire, Match Referee or any other person (including a spectator) during an International Match.Note: Any form of inappropriate physical contact is prohibited in cricket. Without limitation, Players will breach this regulation if they deliberately, recklessly and/or negligently walk or run into or shoulder another Player or Umpire.When assessing the seriousness of the breach, the following factors (without limitation) shall be taken into account: (i) the context of the particular situation, including, without limitation, whether the contact was deliberate (i.e. intentional), reckless, negligent, and/or avoidable; (ii) the force of the contact; (iii) any resulting injury to the person with whom contact was made; and (iv) the person with whom contact was made. "
Article Summary: Asitha Fernando dismissed Yashasvi Jaiswal off the last delivery of the 17th over. The left-hander started walking back to the dressing room when something during the animated send-off triggered him, and he instantly returned. The 24-year-old charged toward the bowler, making visible contact with Fernando's head.

Article Title: Watch: Max Verstappen’s horrific Dutch GP crash as Lando Norris wins chaotic race
Article Text:
Max Verstappen’s horrific crash (Video grab)

Watch the horrific crash and Hülkenberg’s incredible escape:

Norris keeps title hopes alive

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A horrific first-lap crash brought Max Verstappen’s Dutch Grand Prix to a premature end on Sunday, with the four-time Formula 1 world champion walking away unhurt after his Red Bull was sent spinning into the barriers in front of his home fans.Verstappen was running seventh when he appeared to lose control while trying to correct a slide through the final corner on the damp track. His car speared into the barrier on the opposite side of the circuit before sliding back across the track and hitting another wall, scattering debris across the racing surface.The dramatic crash immediately brought out the red flag and halted the race. Verstappen, who had started his final Dutch Grand Prix for the foreseeable future, quickly reassured his team over the radio.“I’m OK,” he said, while also apologising to the Red Bull team.The heavy impact forced a delay of around half an hour as marshals cleared Verstappen’s wrecked car and debris from the circuit. The incident also produced another frightening moment moments later.Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto spun across the track in a cloud of tyre smoke, leaving teammate Nico Hülkenberg with almost no time to react.Hülkenberg made a lightning-quick evasive move to avoid what could have been a huge T-bone collision.“It was crazy with Gabi, I almost T-boned him,” Hülkenberg said over team radio.Verstappen later admitted that he had simply misjudged his speed on the damp surface after rain before the race.The crash proved particularly painful for the Dutch fans, who had turned out in large numbers to cheer their home hero. The Dutch Grand Prix is dropping off the Formula 1 calendar after this season, making Verstappen’s early exit an especially cruel ending to his final home race for now.While Verstappen’s afternoon ended almost immediately, Lando Norris turned the chaotic race into a major boost for his title defence.The McLaren driver started from pole but lost the lead to Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli at the restart following Verstappen’s crash. Norris gradually reeled him in before making a daring move around the outside of the first corner on lap 54 of 72.He completed the pass and took the lead from Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton later that lap, holding on despite running on older tyres to secure his second consecutive victory after his Budapest triumph.“This fight is still on,” Norris told his team over the radio after taking the chequered flag.“I knew I was not going to get many chances. Every lap I spent behind him my chances got lower and lower,” Norris said of his decisive move on Antonelli.Antonelli finished second, ahead of teammate George Russell, while Hamilton was fourth. Charles Leclerc was fifth, followed by Oscar Piastri, Liam Lawson, Hülkenberg, Fernando Alonso and Pierre Gasly.Antonelli’s championship lead now stands at 59 points over Russell and Hamilton, while Norris moved into fourth place.
Article Summary: Max Verstappen crashes out of Dutch Grand Prix in front of home fans. Red Bull driver was running seventh when he lost control of his car. Kimi Antonelli takes lead from Lewis Hamilton at the restart. Lando Norris takes second consecutive victory to keep title hopes alive.

Article Title: Tom Brady’s Las Vegas Raiders role comes under fire as NFL analyst questions his commitment ahead of 2026 season
Article Text:
Tom Brady faces fresh questions over his Raiders role and commitment. (Image via: Imagn Images)

Tom Brady’s influence has grown, but the Raiders have struggled to turn it into results

Tom Brady’s FOX role keeps the conflict question alive around the Raiders

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tom Brady’s role with the Las Vegas Raiders is facing fresh questions ahead of the 2026 NFL season. The seven-time Super Bowl champion became a minority owner with a promise of having a major voice in the organization. But after a 3-14 season, another coaching change and a front office shake-up, NFL analyst Mike Florio believes Brady’s divided attention could become a bigger concern.When Brady’s minority ownership was approved, Raiders owner Mark Davis made his expectations clear, saying: “I want Tom to have a huge voice…no question about it.”Brady has since been involved during a major period of change in Las Vegas. The Raiders moved on from general manager Tom Telesco and head coach Antonio Pierce before replacing them with John Spytek and Pete Carroll. Brady was also reported to have played a role in Davis’ decision to make those changes.The results, however, did not match the level of influence surrounding Brady. The Raiders finished the 2025 season at 3-14, the worst record in the NFL, and earned the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.Carroll then lasted only one season in Las Vegas. Brady also reportedly wanted Ben Johnson to become the Raiders’ head coach, but Johnson ultimately chose the Chicago Bears.That has added another layer to questions about Brady’s influence. Despite the major changes around the team, the Raiders have yet to show that his involvement can produce a clear turnaround.Florio believes the bigger issue is whether Brady can give the Raiders the level of commitment needed to change their direction.“Stop talking about the (Tom) Brady stuff,” said Florio. “Stop talking about it. He’s not going to make him any better as long as he’s doing all this other s**t. So, let him keep doing what he’s doing. Let him think that he’s in a position to turn this thing around because he’s not. I’m more worried about Matt Ryan, I was told, than I am Tom Brady. Because Matt Ryan loaded up the truck and moved to Atlanta. He’s there. He didn’t try to do both jobs. He’s all in, all the time.”Brady’s work as FOX’s lead NFL analyst has created another issue because of his ownership stake. When the league approved his ownership, restrictions were placed on his access to certain Raiders activities and information because of concerns surrounding his broadcasting role.The conflict became especially visible in September 2025 when Brady was seen wearing a headset in the Raiders’ coach’s booth during a game against the Los Angeles Chargers.Florio also compared Brady’s situation with Troy Aikman, who works as a consultant for the Miami Dolphins, while pointing to Matt Ryan’s decision to leave CBS before joining the Atlanta Falcons as president of football operations.“You got to be all in, all the time to be effective. Now, (Troy) Aikman’s in a different spot because he’s not pretending to be the GM or an owner. He’s just kind of an agent out in the field. He’s a traveling salesman for the Dolphins. But is it a conflict? Yes. Should the NFL have never allowed it? Absolutely. They should never have allowed it. ‘Our team’s afraid of Tom Brady helping the Raiders turn it around.’ They’re not. ”Brady has also acknowledged the Raiders’ disappointing performance, saying: “There’s nobody who did a good job.”As the 2026 season approaches, Brady’s role will remain under close attention. His influence over the Raiders is clear, but the team’s results will ultimately determine whether that influence is helping move the franchise forward.
Article Summary: Tom Brady’s role with the Las Vegas Raiders is facing fresh questions ahead of the 2026 NFL season. The seven-time Super Bowl champion became a minority owner with a promise of having a major voice in the organization. But after a 3-14 season, another coaching change and a front office shake-up, NFL analyst Mike Florio believes Brady's divided attention could become a bigger concern.

Article Title: Inspiring story on motherhood: "It's probably the hardest thing I've ever done in my life...it's the most daunting task" - How Donna Kelce navigated the challenges of raising Jason and Travis Kelce
Article Text:
Jason Kelce, Donna Kelce and Travis Kelce (Getty Images)

Donna Kelce’s powerful words about motherhood

Glamour group interview published on October 3, 2024

Raising Jason and Travis Kelce was never just about football

Donna Kelce was also building a career

The values behind Jason and Travis Kelce’s success

Why Donna Kelce’s motherhood confession still resonates

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Donna Kelce, motherhood was never simply about getting her children through childhood. It meant working hard, making difficult choices and giving Jason and Travis Kelce the freedom to discover who they were. Years before they became NFL stars, she was a working mother trying to keep family life steady. In 2024, she opened up about just how demanding that journey had been.Donna Kelce shared her candid thoughts on motherhood during a. The conversation was part of Glamour’s 2024 Women of the Year feature, which brought together Donna, Tina Knowles, Maggie Baird and Mandy Teefey to discuss raising children who would eventually become major figures in sports, music and entertainment.Asked about what motherhood had been like for her, Donna did not describe it as an effortless or glamorous experience. Instead, she focused on the responsibility that comes with raising children who depend on you for almost everything.She said:“Being a mom is probably the hardest thing I’ve ever done in my life. It’s so much easier to just go to work.”..Donna Kelce then explained that raising children means trying to make the best choices possible while dealing with limited resources and the constant responsibility of caring for people who rely on you.She ultimately described motherhood as the most daunting task she had ever taken on.The honesty in her answer is striking because it came from someone whose sons would later become two of the most recognizable names in American football. Yet Donna was not talking about fame when she made the comment. She was talking about the everyday work of being a mother.That distinction matters.Jason Kelce and Travis Kelce did not begin their childhoods with a clear path toward professional football. Donna told Glamour that the brothers tried several sports, including hockey, lacrosse and basketball. Football came later, when they reached seventh grade.Even then, Donna did not immediately know that her sons would build professional careers from the sport.She said the possibility became clearer only when college recruiting letters began arriving. Until that point, she was simply watching two athletic boys grow, compete and find interests of their own.That detail gives her motherhood comments more weight.The woman who eventually became known around the NFL as “Mama Kelce” was not raising two guaranteed stars. She was raising children without knowing where their talents would eventually take them. Her job was to give them room to grow while keeping them grounded.Donna has also spoken about the energetic nature of her sons as children. During the same Glamour conversation, she recalled broken windows and calls from neighbors, while making clear that Jason and Travis were not bad children. They were simply energetic and, as she put it, rambunctious.Those memories offer a very different picture from the polished image fans now see.Before the Super Bowl appearances, championship celebrations and packed stadiums, there were ordinary family moments. There were mistakes, sports practices, neighborhood adventures and the countless small responsibilities that come with raising children.Another important part of Donna’s story is that motherhood did not happen in isolation.She was also working.Donna had a career in banking and later described herself as a major breadwinner in her family. She told Glamour that she worked extremely hard because she wanted to move forward professionally. At the same time, she believed it was important for her children to see that a woman could build a career and pursue her own ambitions.That balance adds another layer to her comments about motherhood.For Donna, going to work could be demanding, but parenting carried a different kind of responsibility. A job has defined duties, deadlines and hours. Raising children is far less predictable. It follows you home. It changes as children grow. And there is no simple measure for whether you are doing it right.Her reflections also touched on her marriage to Ed Kelce. Donna said the couple knew their marriage was no longer working but chose to remain together for their children for a period of time. She described their relationship as friendly and said they wanted to keep life as normal as possible for Jason and Travis.Eventually, Donna said she had to move forward on her own.That part of her story shows that her definition of motherhood was not limited to the visible moments. It included personal sacrifices and decisions that her sons may not have fully understood while they were growing up.Donna Kelce’s influence becomes easier to understand when looking at how she talks about her sons today.She has consistently emphasized supporting children rather than forcing them into a particular future. In the Glamour interview, she explained that parents learn more about their children as they encounter people and experiences outside their immediate community. Her approach was to support what her children loved and encourage them to enjoy it.That philosophy appears to have shaped the Kelce family.Jason eventually became a Super Bowl champion with the Philadelphia Eagles and one of the most respected centers of his generation. Travis established himself as one of the NFL’s premier tight ends with the Kansas City Chiefs.Their achievements are enormous. But Donna's comments suggest that she measures success differently.For her, keeping her sons grounded mattered just as much as celebrating their accomplishments.She told Glamour that she would remind Jason and Travis of their childhood when fame became overwhelming. The goal was simple: remind them where they came from and help them remember that they were still the same people they had always been.That perspective became especially meaningful as both brothers entered a world where almost every part of their lives could attract public attention.Donna Kelce’s description of motherhood stands out because it cuts through the glamour surrounding her family.Today, Jason and Travis are household names. Their games attract millions of viewers, their personal lives generate constant headlines and their family has become part of the wider sports conversation.But Donna’s story began somewhere much quieter.It began with a mother working, raising two boys and trying to make good decisions without knowing exactly where those decisions would lead.Her statement to Glamour was powerful because she did not present motherhood as a perfect journey. She acknowledged the pressure, uncertainty and sacrifice involved. She also recognized that the work of raising children often happens without applause.That may be the most revealing part of her story.The world sees the Super Bowl rings, the records and the stadium lights. Donna remembers the years before all of that. She remembers the children who needed her, the choices she had to make and the effort required to help them become independent adults.Her famous sons may now be the stars, but Donna’s words offer a reminder that behind many extraordinary careers is a much more ordinary story: a parent showing up, day after day, and doing the best they can.And for Donna Kelce, that was the hardest job of all.
Article Summary: Donna Kelce opened up about motherhood during a Glamour group interview. She said: “Being a mom is probably the hardest thing I’ve ever done in my life. It’s so much easier to just go to work.”

Randy Orton and Drew McIntyre are two of the most recognizable veterans still active in WWE , and their careers span different generations and financial trajectories. Orton has spent the last 20-plus years establishing himself as a main event fixture, while McIntyre rebuilt his career after leaving WWE before returning as a major singles star.WWE contracts, bonuses, merchandise royalties and private investments are not fully disclosed so vary widely, says Celebrity Net Worth. McIntyre's WWE deal is said to be in the ballpark of $8 million per year, while Orton's current deal is said to be at a much higher level than his previous salary estimates.The difference between Randy Orton and Drew McIntyre is that Randy Orton has more wealth but Drew McIntyre has been on fire lately. Randy Orton has had the longest continuous run as a premium attraction for WWE, and his financial profile has been boosted by multiple world title reigns, major event appearances, merchandise sales and outside projects. However, published estimates today vary significantly, with Celebrity Net Worth putting Orton at $7 million and other 2026 estimates around $12 million to $15 million.Drew McIntyre’s estimates also differ. Sports Illustrated has his net worth between $2 million and $5 million and an annual salary of $8 million.NDTV estimates his net worth to be around $9 million in 2026. The differences are why net worth figures for WWE performers should be considered estimates, not audited financial statements.Randy Orton’s fortune has been built on incredible longevity. He arrived in WWE in the early 2000s and transitioned from the “Legend Killer” to one of the most established main-event stars in the company. His 14 world title reigns, long rivalries and repeated appearances at WrestleMania have helped keep his commercial value alive.The previous salary reports had Orton in the $4 million-$4.5 million per year range. More recent reports from Celebrity Net Worth state that his current WWE deal is considerably more lucrative, with figures approaching $10 million per year. In 2026, Orton revealed that he still had four years left on his WWE contract, but the company has not disclosed the financials.Drew McIntyre’s financial path has been a different one. He was released by WWE in 2014 and spent time repairing his reputation away from the company, before returning in 2017. His second WWE run saw him win big titles such as the WWE Championship and prove himself as a dependable main event wrestler.And his 2024 contract renewal was reported to have turned him into a payer. Celebrity Net Worth reports that the deal is in the ballpark of $8 million per year, making McIntyre one of WWE’s higher-paid active performers. While NDTV calls the deal a huge financial boost for the Scottish star, Sports Illustrated also reports the figure of $8 million per year.WWE stars both benefit from the value of their recognizable wrestling identities. Their lifestyles also reflect the income of WWE's longtime headliners. Both have access to luxury homes, cars and other high-value purchases, but detailed current valuations are largely private. That makes it more accurate to compare their publicly reported income from wrestling and longevity in the business than to give exact figures for all of their personal assets.In most 2026 estimates, Randy Orton has a stronger accumulated wealth position overall, mostly because of his incredible longevity, championship resume and WWE earning power over time. Drew McIntyre has greatly improved his financial trajectory with his latest contract and continued status as a premium WWE performer; if McIntyre were to stick with his current pay rate for the duration of his contract, the gap could close even more, but Orton's decades-long financial advantage remains significant.

Article Title: Inspiring story on mental health: “It’s a big thing for men to be able to talk and speak their feelings and be vulnerable” - How Travis Kelce delivered a powerful reminder that men do not have to suff
Article Text:
Travis Kelce’s powerful message about men and mental health

Kansas City Chiefs training-camp media session in St. Joseph, Missouri, on August 1, 2022

Why Travis Kelce connected vulnerability with brotherhood

Travis Kelce showed that vulnerability can be a form of strength

Travis Kelce’s message still matters beyond the Chiefs locker room

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Travis Kelce has built a reputation around confidence, intensity and leadership. Yet one of his most meaningful messages had little to do with football. In August 2022, the Kansas City Chiefs tight end spoke openly about why men need people they can trust enough to discuss their feelings with. His words offered a reminder that vulnerability does not weaken a man. Sometimes, it is what makes a teammate, brother or friend stronger.Kelce made the remarks during a. KMBC published the comments the following day.The conversation was rooted in football, but Kelce's answer reached far beyond the locker room.He said:“It’s a big thing for men to be able to talk and you know, speak their feelings to, especially to the ones next to them and you know, be vulnerable in those moments.”That short statement carries a surprisingly large message.For years, many men have been taught, directly or indirectly, to hide discomfort. They are often expected to remain calm, tough and in control even when life becomes difficult. Saying that something hurts can feel like admitting weakness. Asking for help can feel even harder.Kelce pushed against that idea.He suggested that men should be able to speak honestly with the people standing beside them.In his world, that means teammates. Outside football, it can mean brothers, friends, partners, coaches or anyone who has earned a person's trust.His point was not that men should constantly talk about their problems. It was that they should not feel ashamed when they need to.The rest of Kelce's answer made his philosophy even clearer. He described emotional openness as part of what it means to be a brother, mentor and good teammate. He also explained that he tries to encourage this kind of supportive atmosphere among the people around him.That idea fits naturally into a professional sports environment.An NFL locker room can be an intense place. Players compete for jobs, deal with injuries, handle public criticism and spend much of their lives under enormous pressure. They are expected to perform even when something outside football is weighing on them.Kelce appeared to understand that a strong team cannot be built only through physical talent.Trust matters. So does friendship.And sometimes, the most important conversation between teammates has nothing to do with the next opponent.Kelce's words suggested that emotional support should not be treated as something separate from leadership. Instead, he viewed it as part of being a responsible teammate. Someone who notices when another person is struggling can offer support before that struggle becomes even heavier.That is a lesson that applies far beyond the NFL.The idea of vulnerability can sound uncomfortable, particularly when discussing professional athletes.Football rewards toughness. Players are praised for playing through pain and maintaining composure under pressure. But emotional strength and emotional silence are not the same thing.Kelce's comments offered a different definition of toughness.Being willing to say, “I'm struggling,” requires honesty. Being willing to listen to someone else requires patience. And creating an environment where another man feels safe enough to open up requires trust.Those qualities do not make someone less strong. They can make relationships stronger.A later mental-health feature from Grow Strong KC highlighted Kelce's remarks in the context of the stigma surrounding men's mental health. The article noted that men can be less likely to seek mental-health treatment and that stigma can become a major barrier to asking for support.That context gives Kelce's 2022 comments even more relevance.He was not presenting himself as a mental-health expert. He was speaking from the perspective of a teammate and leader. His message was much simpler: men should have people they can talk to.Sometimes that is where change begins.What makes Kelce's comments memorable is their lack of drama.He did not deliver a complicated speech. He simply described something he believed mattered.Men need room to talk. They need people who will listen. They need friendships where honesty is not mistaken for weakness.And they need environments where vulnerability does not become a reason for ridicule.Kelce also framed this as part of mentorship. His view was that a good mentor does more than teach someone how to perform. A good mentor helps create an environment where people can become better versions of themselves.That is particularly important for younger athletes.A young player entering professional football may believe that showing emotion will damage his reputation. Seeing an established star speak openly about vulnerability can challenge that assumption.It sends another message: you can be competitive and compassionate. You can be confident and still admit when something is difficult. You can lead without pretending that you have everything figured out.Kelce's comments also fit a broader conversation that has become increasingly important in sports. Athletes are people before they are performers. Their physical health matters, but so does their emotional well-being.The pressure does not disappear simply because someone plays in front of thousands of fans.In fact, fame can create another layer of pressure. That is why having trusted people nearby matters.For Kelce, the answer appeared to be the people beside him. His teammates were not simply colleagues competing for the same championship. They could also be friends, mentors and sources of support.That may be the most powerful part of his message.The NFL star who is known for his loud personality and fearless style was also reminding men that they do not always have to be loud about their struggles.Sometimes, strength looks like opening up. Sometimes, leadership begins with listening. And sometimes, the most important thing a man can say is simply how he feels.
Article Summary: Travis Kelce spoke openly about why men need people they can trust enough to discuss their feelings with. He suggested that men should be able to speak honestly with the people standing beside them. In his world, that means teammates. Outside football, it can mean brothers, friends, partners, coaches.

Article Title: Tom Brady’s son Jack Moynahan refuses to follow his father’s football footsteps as basketball breakout grabs attention
Article Text:
Jack Moynahan draws attention at The Newman School

Tom Brady’s son chooses basketball over football
