Tom Brady’s oldest son is stepping into the spotlight for a reason that has little to do with football. Jack Moynahan, the former NFL star’s 19-year-old son, is drawing fresh attention after showcasing his basketball skills at The Newman School in Boston. Standing at 6-foot-6, Jack is beginning to build a sporting identity of his own, and fans are already eager to see how far his talent can take him.Jack Moynahan’s recent appearance on the basketball court has sparked plenty of excitement around his future. The Newman School shared footage of him on social media, highlighting the 6-foot-6 forward as a player to watch in the Class of 2027.The reaction was immediate. Supporters praised Jack’s confidence and appearance on the court, with one fan writing, “Bro looks more like Tom Brady than Tom Brady,” while another kept it simple with, “Smooth.”Other comments were even more enthusiastic, including “Yessir Jack!!!!🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥,” and “Let’s go Jack.” One supporter also pointed out Jack’s resemblance to his famous father, writing, “Second to last slide. That glare. He indeed is his father’s son.”The attention is notable because Jack has never appeared especially interested in following Tom Brady into football. Instead, basketball has gradually become a much bigger part of his sporting life.Jack was born to Tom Brady and actress Bridget Moynahan in 2007, shortly after their relationship ended. Despite growing up with one of football’s most recognizable names as his father, Jack has been allowed to explore his own interests rather than being pushed toward the NFL.Moynahan previously spoke about her son’s athletic preferences and made it clear that basketball was among his strongest interests.“He’s kinda like that normal kid who doesn’t really know what he wants to do yet. And I think that’s OK, and I certainly don’t want to put any pressure on him to do what I do or what his father does,” Bridget said, before adding, “He’s more of a basketball player…Yeah, basketball and lacrosse right now.”That freedom could prove important as Jack develops his game. His 6-foot-6 frame gives him an obvious physical advantage, while his experience with competitive basketball suggests that he is taking the sport seriously.Jack has also been seen around NBA talent. In 2025, he was photographed with New York Knicks star Karl-Anthony Towns while Tom Brady watched from the court. Those moments offered another glimpse into the young athlete’s growing connection to basketball.For Brady, whose career was defined by football, watching his children pursue different sports may be a different kind of victory. Jack does not need to become the next Tom Brady. If his recent performances are any indication, he may be busy creating a name that belongs entirely to him.
Article Summary: Jack Moynahan, the former NFL star’s 19-year-old son, is drawing fresh attention after showcasing his basketball skills at The Newman School in Boston. Standing at 6-foot-6, Jack is beginning to build a sporting identity of his own and fans are eager to see how far his talent can take him.

Article Title: 21 former captains, including Gavaskar and Kapil, renew appeal over Imran Khan's medical treatment
Article Text:
Kapil Dev and Sunil Gavaskar (Image credit: Agencies)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: As many as 21 former international captains from nine cricketing nations, including India’s Sunil Gavaskar Kapil Dev and Dilip Vengsarkar, have written to Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, renewing their appeal for the medical treatment and welfare of Pakistan’s former Prime Minister and 1992 World Cup-winning captain Imran Khan , following developments this week that they say fall short of a directive of the Supreme Court of the country.The letter — a follow-up to one sent in February by 14 former captains — was prompted by events surrounding a Supreme Court order that Khan be transferred to hospital for examination by a medical board including his own physicians and his sister, Dr Uzma Khan, alongside reinstated weekly family visits.The 73-year-old Imran is currently facing severe health issues after having been in jail for more than three years following his tenure as Pakistan PM.On Friday, Imran returned to Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail shortly after undergoing a medical examination at Shifa Hospital in Islamabad.In February this year, 14 legendary captains from five countries — including Gavaskar, Kapil Dev and Greg Chappell, a former head coach of Team India — had made a fervent, emotional appeal to the Pakistan government about ensuring proper treatment for Imran, amid mounting concerns about the cricketing icon’s health.However, there was no response from the Pakistan government to the cricket legends’ request.In the latest letter (a copy is with TOI), addressed to the Pakistan PM and titled "Appeal by 21 Former International Cricket Captains on the Medical Treatment and Welfare of Imran Khan," Chappell & Co. have written, “Dear Prime Minister, six months ago, fourteen former international cricket captains wrote to you and the Pakistani government appealing for humane treatment and proper medical care for Imran Khan. We wrote then not as politicians, but as former colleagues and rivals who share a bond forged on the cricket field — one that transcends the borders and disputes that too often divide countries.“We write again now — joined by seven further former captains — because of what has reportedly just occurred. Pakistan’s Supreme Court ordered that Imran Khan be transferred to hospital for examination by a medical board that was to include his own personal physicians and his sister, Dr Uzma Khan. The Court also reinstated weekly family visits. These were very welcome steps.Concerningly, Mr Khan’s hospital stay lasted only a few hours. He was examined by a state-appointed team rather than the board the Court had directed, declared “medically fit,” and returned to Adiala Jail before that board could complete its work. His family and legal team say this falls short of what the court ordered.The signatories, who describe themselves as writing "not as politicians, but as former colleagues and rivals who share a bond forged on the cricket field," are careful to note they do not seek to adjudicate Pakistan's domestic legal processes. Their letter makes three specific requests: that the Court-directed medical board be permitted to complete its independent assessment; that weekly family visits continue without interruption; and that any treatment the assessment recommends be provided without delay."We're not asking Pakistan for anything unusual — just that a court order most countries would take for granted is actually carried out," said Greg Chappell, who took this initiative."We do not presume to adjudicate Pakistan’s domestic legal processes. That is not our place, and it was not the spirit in which we wrote in February. But we do ask, again, respectfully: 1. That the medical board directed by the Supreme Court — including Mr Khan’s own doctors — be permitted to complete a full and independent assessment of his health, particularly the reported loss of vision in his right eye. 2. That the weekly family visits reinstated by the Court be honoured without interruption or administrative delay.3. That whatever the outcome of that medical assessment, the treatment recommended by it be provided without delay. Imran Khan is 73 years old and has now spent more than three years in custody. Whatever the legal and political arguments surrounding his case, the basic decency of ensuring a court-ordered medical process is actually completed is not, in our view, a controversial request. It is one we believe every nation that plays this game would recognise as fair. We hope this matter can be resolved expeditiously and with the dignity Mr Imran Khan deserves. Yours in cricket,"Also among the signatories of the letter are Michael Atherton, Alex Blackwell, Allan Border, Michael Brearley, Greg Chappell, Ian Chappell, Belinda Clark, Alastair Cook, Lee Germon, Adam Gilchrist, David Gower, Kim Hughes, Nasser Hussain, Clive Lloyd, Arjuna Ranatunga, Andrew Strauss, Steve Waugh and John Wright.
Article Summary: As many as 21 former international captains have written to Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. They are renewing their appeal for the medical treatment and welfare of Imran Khan. The letter is a follow-up to one sent in February by 14 former captains.

Article Title: How Bangladesh's loss to Australia boosts India's WTC final hopes
Article Text:
L-R: Ajit Agarkar, Gautam Gambhir, Shubman Gill, and Sitanshu Kotak. (PTI Photo)

Bangladesh's loss opens door for India

Bangladesh make ranking history despite defeat

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Bangladesh's defeat to Australia in the second Test in Mackay has given India a small but significant boost in the race for a place in the World Test Championship (WTC) final.Bangladesh had stunned Australia in the opening Test in Darwin to secure their first-ever Test win Down Under, but Mitchell Starc's 10-wicket match haul inspired the hosts to an innings-and-51-run victory in the second Test on Sunday. The result not only allowed Australia to level the series 1-1 but also cost Bangladesh valuable points in the WTC standings.India, currently fifth in the nine-team table, can now move above Bangladesh and reclaim fourth place by beating Sri Lanka in the second Test in Colombo.Bangladesh remain fourth despite the defeat, but their points percentage (PCT) has dropped sharply from 66.67 after their Darwin victory to 55.56. They now have 50 points from six matches, with three wins, two defeats and one draw.India are just behind them with 64 points and a PCT of 53.33 from 10 matches. Shubman Gill's side have five wins, four defeats and one draw.The equation is straightforward for India: a victory over Sri Lanka in Colombo will take them past Bangladesh and into fourth place.Australia strengthened their position at the top with 96 points and an 80 PCT from 10 matches, while South Africa are second with a 75 PCT and New Zealand third with 72.22.Sri Lanka, India's current opponents, are sixth with a PCT of 33.33. England, West Indies and Pakistan occupy the next three positions.India's bigger challenge, however, is that they need to continue winning consistently to stay in contention for the top two positions that ultimately determine the finalists.Bangladesh's Test campaign has still produced a landmark achievement. Despite losing the second Test, they climbed three places to No.6 in the latest ICC Test rankings — their highest-ever position."Of course (reaching No. 6) is good news," Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto said after the Mackay defeat. "I am just hearing about it. To reach No 6 in the Test ranking is a huge achievement. It would have been better if we could have played better cricket in this Test match."Shanto also called for Bangladesh to play more frequently in Australia after their first Test series there in 23 years."We are here after 23 years (first Test series in Australia since 2003). It's not easy to compete in this condition against this quality of team. If we are able to come here consistently, then the players can get an idea of playing here. They will have more experience playing in Australia. They can adjust to this kind of condition and play good cricket," he said."It's hard for the players. Probably 90% of the players haven't played here. They don't know how to adjust, how to cope with this kind of condition, and this kind of bowling attack. My request is that we want to play here. We want to play similar kind of conditions consistently, not after 23 or 25 years," he added.
Article Summary: Bangladesh's defeat to Australia in Mackay has given India a boost in the race for a place in the World Test Championship final. India, currently fifth in the nine-team table, can now move above Bangladesh and reclaim fourth place by beating Sri Lanka in the second Test in Colombo. Australia strengthened their position at the top with 96 points and an 80 PCT from 10 matches.

Article Title: ‘Unacceptable’: Justin Langer slams two-day Tests after Australia rout Bangladesh
Article Text:
Australia beat Bangladesh in two days. (Pic credit: CA)

Langer blames batting technique

'Bangladesh need more overseas Tests'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Australia opener Justin Langer has slammed the increasing frequency of Test matches ending inside two days, calling the trend “unacceptable” after Australia wrapped up an innings-and-51-run victory over Bangladesh in Mackay on Sunday.Australia needed only 750 balls to complete the second Test, bouncing back from their shock nine-wicket defeat in Darwin to level the two-match series 1-1. The result also marked the third Test involving Australia in their last seven to finish inside two days, raising fresh concerns over the health of the longest format.“Two-day Test matches (are) unacceptable. It's no good for the game for so many reasons. Last year was disappointing for the crowds, for the kids who get to watch their heroes on TV or listen on the radio or get to the ground,” Langer said on SEN Radio.Langer, who played 105 Tests for Australia, also highlighted the financial consequences of matches ending prematurely.“Economically it's a disaster for Cricket Australia who put money into grassroots cricket. And you know we're talking about very well-paid professionals now, and you get tired of hearing ‘Oh it's just the pitches, oh it's the curators, it's the ball moves a bit’,” he said.Bangladesh were bowled out for 64 in their first innings and 95 in their second, while Mitchell Starc claimed 10 wickets in the match. Langer, however, believes the problem goes beyond pitch conditions and points towards shortcomings in batting fundamentals.“I think a lot of it is down to basic batting technique. Take this test match alone. Almost every dismissal has been batters; their front foot has not gone past the front line. It's just basic technique, and it's footwork patterns.“I coach young guys now, and I've just come back from England; there are a couple of batters who are in our Hundred team who are also wanting to become Test players. And you have some hits with them, and you say some things to them which are so basic for us in the game, and their eyes light up like you're teaching them magic for the first time,” he added.Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto admitted his side did not produce their best performance but said the series would provide valuable lessons.“Yeah, obviously I think we all know how good they are and, as I said in the press conference, they have been experienced for almost 50, more than 50 years. So yeah, they played, they showed their character, and as the Bangladesh Test team, we didn’t play our best match,” Shanto said.He acknowledged the challenging conditions in Mackay, where extra bounce and movement made batting difficult.“Yeah, obviously I think this is a different condition, and there is a little bit more extra bounce and swing in the air. So it’s challenging for us. But as a team, if we want to go forward, we need to adjust to this condition, and I hope this experience will help going forward,” he said. Shoriful Islam 's 7/48 was a major positive for Bangladesh, while Shanto also praised Taskin Ahmed and Hasan Mahmud.“It’s quite difficult for all the batters. If you look at their batting also, they also struggled and the way Shoriful, Taskin and Hasan bowled, really happy to see them and it’s quite a difficult wicket to bat, to be very honest,” he said.Bangladesh's historic Darwin victory provided a glimpse of their potential, and Shanto called for more exposure overseas.“Yeah, obviously I think it’s a very proud moment as a team, and we showed our character, and we were disciplined, as you mentioned, in the first Test, and we need to be consistent. I believe if we are able to get more chances, similar kind of conditions here, it will help us, and that’s what we want,” he said.“Not long, long term, like 23 years of coming here and playing two Test matches. It’s not easy. So if we have that chance to play every single year, it will help us to improve our game,” he said.
Article Summary: Australia beat Bangladesh by an innings and 51 runs in second Test in Mackay. Third Test involving Australia in last seven to finish inside two days. Justin Langer says trend is 'unacceptable' and blames batting technique. Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto says series will provide valuable lessons.

Article Title: 'There is no point in playing anymore': Karn Sharma, winner of 4 IPL titles, retires from all forms of cricket
Article Text:
Bengaluru: Royal Challengers Bangalore player Karn Sharma during a training session ahead of the Indian Premier League (IPL) 2024 cricket tournament, at M. Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru. (PTI Photo/Shailendra Bhojak)

A career filled with achievements

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Looking ahead

Former India leg-spinner Karn Sharma has retired from all forms of cricket at the age of 38, bringing an end to a career that lasted more than two decades.Sharma played one Test, two ODIs and one T20I for India, with his last international appearance coming in November 2014.“My station has arrived, I am already 38 and I feel there is no point in playing anymore. The more I play, I will occupy the place of a young player in the team. There is no point in staying in playing when you know that India call will never come. So I spoke to my family and friends and they said, it’s the right time,” Sharma told The Indian Express.Sharma made his only Test appearance against Australia in Adelaide in 2014. He later found it difficult to return to the national team as R Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja became established in India's spin department.Despite that, Sharma looks back at his career with satisfaction. He played 97 First-Class matches, taking 270 wickets, and represented Uttar Pradesh, Railways, Vidarbha and Andhra. He also featured in more than 90 IPL matches for Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Mumbai Indians, Sunrisers Hyderabad and Chennai Super Kings, winning four IPL titles.“God gave me everything which I never dreamt of. When I began to play cricket, my dream was always to play for India and play all three formats for the Indian team.There are very few players who play all three formats. I did all the hard work, gave all I had. Somewhere in destiny it was written that I will play these games and am happy. I want to thank everyone, my family, friends, coaches, trainers, various Ranji and IPL sides.Physios, trainers and groundsmen, all played a part in my career,” he added.Sharma said receiving his India Test cap remains one of the most memorable moments of his career.“Getting a Test cap remains a special place in my heart. It was the best day for sure. Playing for India and learning I got will hold a special place for sure. Everytime I played, I gave it all I had, I always tried to learn and improve. The time has come for me to say goodbye and sign off cap number 283,” he explains.He has no immediate plans after retirement but wants to remain connected with cricket.“I don’t know, it will be hard to say at the moment but I want to give back to the game. If someone needs my help, I will be there. I will be going into my second innings of my life post retirement, will see what opportunities come my way,” he said.
Article Summary: Former India leg-spinner Karn Sharma has retired from all forms of cricket. Sharma played one Test, two ODIs and one T20I for India, with his last international appearance coming in November 2014. He played 97 First Class matches, taking 270 wickets, and represented Uttar Pradesh, Railways, Vidarbha and Andhra.

There was also no video available from the portion of practice where he went down, so there is no reliable visual indication of what happened beyond the eyewitness reports.The Raiders quickly adjusted their backfield after Jeanty left practice. Rookie Mike Washington Jr. moved into first-team work for the remainder of Sunday’s session.Washington had already caught the coaching staff’s attention during the preseason. He rushed for 56 yards against the Houston Texans on August 20 and had earlier produced a 53-yard run against the Arizona Cardinals.After the Texans game on August 20, Washington explained how he approached his growing opportunities.“I’ve just been focused on the present, being where my feet are,” Washington said after the Raiders’ preseason game against Houston. “I’m just going play by play and day by day.”Kubiak also discussed Washington after that game. The Raiders coach said players were “earning roles” and praised the rookie’s work with the football.“Mike’s doing a great job running the ball,” Kubiak said after the August 20 preseason game. “We have to keep getting him better in all facets of his game.”Those words now carry extra significance. Washington was already earning more work before Jeanty went down. If Jeanty misses time, the rookie could move from promising backup to a major part of the Raiders’ offense.For now, though, there is no confirmed diagnosis. The latest Ashton Jeanty injury update remains limited to an apparent right-leg injury, an inability to put weight on the leg and an emotional reaction from his teammates.The Raiders now await the medical news that will determine their next move at running back.
Article Summary: Ashton Jeanty suffered an apparent right-leg injury during the Las Vegas Raiders’ practice on Sunday, August 23. The second-year running back went down while diving for a low pass from Kirk Cousins. Trainers helped him off the field, and Jeanty could not put weight on his right leg. As of now, the Raiders had not announced a diagnosis of any recovery timeline.

Article Title: Vanessa Bryant shares heartfelt birthday tribute to late husband Kobe Bryant
Article Text:
Vanessa Bryant and Kobe Bryant. Image via: Getty Images

Vanessa Bryant celebrates Lakers legend Kobe Bryant's birthday

Pau Gasol and Magic Johnson lead Lakers family's birthday tributes

Kobe Bryant's story goes on past highlight reels

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kobe Bryant would have turned 48 on Sunday, and his wife Vanessa marked it the only way she knows how, with a photo that says more than any caption could. She shared a throwback shot of them tangled together on a lawn chair, laughing, impossibly young.Six years have passed since Kobe and their daughter Gianna died in a helicopter crash near Calabasas, and the ache clearly has not faded for Vanessa or the basketball world that once orbited around him. Tributes poured in fast, from former teammates to fans still holding on to what he meant.The photo Vanessa Bryant posted showed her sitting on Kobe's lap during a lazy afternoon outdoors, both of them grinning at whoever was holding the camera. Alongside it, she wrote, "Happy birthday, baby. I love you so much," and added his birthdate with a red heart and praying hands.The comments filled up quickly. Candace Parker left a string of hearts. So did Michael Phelps. Natalia, the oldest of Kobe and Vanessa's three daughters, added one of her own. Kris Jenner, Kimora Lee Simmons, Gabrielle Union and David Beckham all showed up too, a reminder of how far Kobe's reach extended beyond basketball.Vanessa has spent the last several years keeping her husband's memory visible without turning it into spectacle, and Sunday's post fit that pattern. It also arrived a few months after she had to publicly shut down a rumor claiming she was pregnant with a boyfriend's child, clarifying she wasn't expecting and wasn't seeing anyone. Kobe and Vanessa met on a music video set back in 1999, got engaged within six months, and married in 2001. Twenty seasons and five championships later, he remains one of the most mourned figures the sport has ever had.Vanessa wasn't the only one posting tributes. Members of the Lakers family used social media to send their own messages, some playful, some raw.Pau Gasol wrote, "Happy birthday hermano, miss you. ❤" (@paugasol)Magic Johnson posted, "I want to wish a happy heavenly birthday to Kobe Bryant!" (@MagicJohnson)Caron Butler kept his short: "Happy Birthday Bean…" (@realtuffjuice)Mychal Thompson sounded almost stunned by the number itself: "WOW…Kobe…48? Ohhhh man weer gettin OLD…I miss Kobe…" (@champagnennuts)The Lakers organization posted simply, "Icon. Legend. Laker. Happy Birthday, Kobe" (@Lakers)Sunday's date carries extra weight for Lakers fans since Aug. 24, the day right after, is recognized as Mamba Day, tied to his two jersey numbers, 8 and 24.What's struck people in the years since Kobe's death is how much of his life outside basketball still gets talked about. He didn't just retire and fade into commentary work. He wrote children's books, launching The Wizenard Series, and found real success doing it, a side of his post-playing career that often gets overshadowed by the championship banners.That's part of why these birthday posts land the way they do. They're not just nostalgia for a jump shot. They're a reminder that Kobe was still building things when his life was cut short, and that the people closest to him, from Vanessa to Gasol to Magic, are still the ones keeping that fuller picture alive.
Article Summary: Kobe Bryant would have turned 48 on Sunday. His wife Vanessa shared a throwback photo of the two of them. The Lakers organization posted simply, "Icon. Laker. Happy Birthday, Kobe" Kris Jenner, Kimora Lee Simmons, Gabrielle Union and David Beckham also posted tributes.

Article Title: D4vd murder investigation: Streamer faces new scrutiny after chilling details about Celeste’s death emerge
Article Text:
D4vd murder case reveals new details about Celeste Rivas Hernandez’s death

D4vd maintains innocence as murder case moves forward

The investigation into Celeste Rivas Hernandez’s death has taken a significant turn with the release of the medical examiner’s findings. The Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner determined that the 15-year-old died from multiple penetrating injuries and classified the death as a homicide. The report had been completed months earlier but remained sealed while investigators continued examining the case.The newly released findings provide the clearest official account yet of the injuries that caused Celeste’s death. According to the medical examiner, the teenager suffered multiple penetrating injuries caused by an object or objects. The examination also identified traumatic injuries, while toxicology testing produced presumptive positive results for benzodiazepines and methamphetamine/MDMA.The report was completed on December 9, 2025, several months after Celeste’s remains were discovered. The medical examiner’s office said a court order had prevented the findings from being released earlier. Officials ultimately made the determination public on April 22, 2026.The circumstances surrounding the discovery made the case particularly disturbing. Celeste’s remains were found inside the front trunk of a vehicle at a Los Angeles tow yard in September 2025.By then, investigators said her body had undergone severe postmortem changes, indicating that significant time had passed since her death.The medical examiner classified the manner of death as homicide. That finding establishes how the death occurred from a forensic perspective, but it does not by itself determine who was responsible.Singer David Anthony Burke, known professionally as D4vd, has been charged with first-degree murder in connection with Celeste’s death. Prosecutors have also brought additional allegations against him, while Burke’s attorneys have strongly rejected the accusations.His legal team said the evidence presented at trial will establish that Burke was not responsible for Celeste’s death."The actual evidence in this case will show that David Burke did not murder Celeste Rivas Hernandez and he was not the cause of her death," his attorneys, Blair Berk, Marilyn Bednarski and Regina Peter, said in a statement on Monday. "We will vigorously defend David's innocence."That position is now set against the medical examiner’s homicide determination and the broader investigation. Burke has pleaded not guilty and remains in custody without bail, according to the case information provided by ABC News.For Celeste’s family, the release of the report has brought painful answers rather than closure. Her parents described their daughter as a “beautiful, strong girl who loved to sing and dance” and said they want justice for her."We love her very much and she always told us that she loved us. We miss her deeply," her parents, Jesus Rivas and Mercedes Martinez, said. "All we want is justice for Celeste."The medical examiner’s findings may become an important piece of evidence as the prosecution and defense prepare their cases. The next stages will focus not only on how Celeste died, but also on what investigators can prove about the events that led to her death. For now, the homicide ruling adds a crucial forensic finding to a case that remains before the courts.
Article Summary: The Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner determined that the 15-year-old died from multiple penetrating injuries and classified the death as a homicide. David Anthony Burke, known professionally as D4vd, has been charged with first-degree murder in connection with Celeste’s death.

Article Title: Twitch streamer Hasan Piker takes aim at Erika Kirk after “We Are Charlie Kirk” controversy: “These guys are all goddamn grifters”
Article Text:
Hasan Piker responds to the Charlie Kirk backlash

Hasan Piker calls critics “grifters” as controversy grows

Hasan Piker has pushed back against the backlash surrounding his recent live-show performance of “We Are Charlie Kirk,” and a screenshot circulating online has added another layer to the controversy. In the clip, the Twitch streamer dismisses the criticism, compares his treatment of Charlie Kirk with that of Erika Kirk, and takes aim at Republicans he says are trying to fill Kirk’s place.The controversy began after Piker was filmed singing “We Are Charlie Kirk” during a Fear& LIVE show. The performance quickly spread online, with critics accusing him of mocking the late conservative activist and turning a deeply sensitive subject into entertainment. Reports place the performance at the Golden Gate Theatre in San Francisco during the opening stretch of the tour.The screenshot shared by Leiga Sapienti captures Piker addressing the reaction during a stream. Rather than backing away from the criticism, he appeared frustrated by what he described as another round of outrage surrounding Kirk. He also rejected the idea that his comments were simply part of a political narrative being pushed against Kirk.Piker then made a striking comparison involving Erika Kirk, Charlie Kirk’s widow, before broadening his criticism to Republicans who have attempted to carry forward Charlie Kirk’s political influence.“You know Trump just handed the Liberals a win in the upcoming Quebec provincial elections. Oh, I know I Know my brain is so fried the fake outrage about Charlie Kirk shit We've been doing it like three times a week 30k people for 10 months. It's not just me doing it. Everyone does it?”The tone of his response highlights why the controversy has continued to attract attention. Piker is not presenting the incident as an isolated joke. Instead, he frames the reaction as part of a much larger cycle of online political outrage.The most provocative part of Piker’s response came when he argued that his approach toward Charlie Kirk was actually more respectful than that of people who publicly aligned themselves with Kirk’s movement.That claim is likely to fuel further debate because it shifts the focus away from the live performance itself and toward the people now associated with Kirk’s political legacy.“If anything, I'm more I'm more respectful to Charlie Kirk than Erica Kirk is I'm more respectful to Charlie Kirk than virtually every goddamn Republican out there who who has Tried to fill his shoes, you know what? I mean? Yeah, these guys are all goddamn grifters anyway”The remarks also come as scrutiny around Piker has intensified following the live performance. Video from the show showed him leading the audience through the song while his co-hosts and members of the crowd reacted around him. The song has become an online meme since emerging after Kirk’s assassination, making Piker’s decision to perform it especially contentious.Piker’s comments now give the controversy a second chapter. Instead of allowing the backlash to fade after the performance, he has directly challenged those criticizing him and questioned the motives of people claiming to defend Kirk’s legacy. Whether that argument changes public opinion remains unclear, but his response has ensured that the debate over the performance will continue far beyond the stage.
Article Summary: Hasan Piker has responded to the backlash surrounding his live-show performance of "We Are Charlie Kirk" The Twitch streamer dismissed the criticism as part of a larger cycle of online political outrage. He also made a striking comparison involving Erika Kirk, Charlie Kirk’s widow.
